Scenario Name: Cart and session state remain deterministic across back, forward, refresh and logout during checkout
Error Log: TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 15000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for getByTestId('react-burger-menu-btn')
Probable Root Cause: Environment/flakiness. The failing click targets BasePage.logout()'s getByTestId('react-burger-menu-btn') on checkout-step-one. The identical locator/timeout signature recurs in three other independent scenarios in this same run (JIRA190-SCN-33, JIRA-1 SCN-34, JIRA-1 SCN-44) across different pages, and JIRA-1's saved error-context.md snapshots for the same locator show the "Open Menu" button present in the final DOM, indicating the element eventually renders but wasn't actionable within 15s - consistent with transient slowness on the shared public saucedemo.com demo site rather than a code defect specific to this test.
Suggested Fix: Re-run this scenario in isolation (outside the full concurrent headed batch) with retries enabled to confirm intermittency; if the click reliably fails even in isolation, escalate to an automation-defect investigation of BasePage.logout() (e.g. add an explicit wait for visible+stable state, or increase the click timeout, before treating it as a real UI defect).

Scenario Name: Rapid double-click on Add to cart does not duplicate the line item
Error Log: Error: expect(locator).toHaveText(expected) failed Locator: getByTestId('shopping-cart-badge') Expected: "1"
Probable Root Cause: Automation defect. InventoryPage.rapidDoubleClickAddToCart() fires two concurrent, unawaited .click() calls via Promise.all() on the same re-queried locator instead of a single click plus an explicit assertion that a second click is a no-op. This inherently racy pattern can produce a non-deterministic outcome (either a genuine double-add or an incidental click-target error) depending on exact timing, and the HTML report's error cell was truncated before the actual "Received" badge value, so it can't be confirmed from this evidence alone whether the app duplicated the item or the test's own race caused the mismatch.
Suggested Fix: Rewrite InventoryPage.rapidDoubleClickAddToCart() to avoid the artificial unawaited race (e.g. click once, then explicitly assert the button is disabled/toggled before attempting a second interaction) and log the actual badge value on failure. Re-run to determine whether the badge reliably shows '2' (a real app race-condition defect worth filing) versus erroring differently each run.

Scenario Name: Postal code field handles boundary-length and whitespace-only input without crashing
Error Log: TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 15000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for getByTestId('inventory-item').filter({ hasText: 'Sauce Labs Backpack' }).getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i })
Probable Root Cause: Automation defect. Case A and Case B both call reachCheckoutStepOne(page, [PRODUCT_1]) on the same shared `page` without ever removing Sauce Labs Backpack from the cart between them. Case A already toggled its "Add to cart" button to "Remove" by adding it to cart and never clearing it (it only submits a 50-char postal code and continues), so Case B's InventoryPage.addProductToCart('Sauce Labs Backpack') call inside addProductsToCart() waits forever for an "Add to cart" button that no longer exists on that product's card - the identical cart-not-reset pattern independently confirmed via JIRA-1's SCN-6/SCN-8 error-context.md artifacts.
Suggested Fix: In tests/JIRA-190.spec.ts, reset cart state between Case A and Case B (e.g. call cartPage.removeItem('Sauce Labs Backpack') at the end of Case A, or give each test.step a fresh browser context) so Case B starts from a known-empty cart before re-adding the product.
